summary: the largest time step the Courant condition allows on a grid

inputs.name: courant_limit
inputs.meaning: the Courant number the scheme is run below; a judgement that depends on the scheme, bound to a row with its own source

inputs.name: cell_size
inputs.meaning: the smallest cell or element of the grid or mesh, along the direction the signal travels

inputs.name: velocity
inputs.meaning: the largest speed at which the solution carries information across the grid: the largest flow velocity for advection, the wave speed for a wave equation

outputs.name: time_step_max
outputs.meaning: the upper bound on the time step from the Courant condition

validity: explicit or semi-implicit time stepping of advection or of waves on a grid or a mesh, whatever program does it; not for a method without a grid (particles, Monte Carlo), where the condition does not arise. The limit itself depends on the scheme and is an input

source.citation: R. Courant, K. Friedrichs, H. Lewy, Über die partiellen Differenzengleichungen der mathematischen Physik, Mathematische Annalen 100 (1928)
source.locus: the condition that the numerical domain of dependence contains the physical one: time step <= C * cell size / velocity

note: v1 with its scope no longer bound to engines by name: v1 named rheotool and openfoam alone, so the Designer offered no Courant bound for a flow on DOLFINx (meta_agent/failures.jsonl cfd-1, run cfd/20261117-1, tasks/019). The relation is the condition of the cited paper and is a property of a time scheme on a grid, not of a program. The code is v1's; the inputs' meanings say what a velocity is for a wave. No value of the source stands behind the worked cases: each is worked by hand in its worked field, one a flow and one an electromagnetic wave, two unrelated kinds.
